newsitem.title: USA: Perry to leave Cabinet -- Pentagon officials.
newsitem.headline: Perry to leave Cabinet -- Pentagon officials.

text.p: Pentagon officials said Defence Secretary William Perry told his staff on Wednesday that he planned to resign, and Perry said he would discuss his future with President Bill Clinton this week.

"I have not submitted a letter of resignation," Perry told reporters at Offutt Air Force Base in Nebraska, lamenting that it had become increasingly difficult in the past year to deal with the Republican-led Congress on a bipartisan basis.
"I have not had a final discussion with the president and have not made a final commitment yet. That will happen this week," said Perry, 69, who has served as defence secretary since early 1994.

He refused to elaborate on his plans, but defence officials in Washington said Perry met with his staff on Wednesday, the day after Clinton was re-elected, to tell them he had already told Clinton he wanted to leave in the coming months.

Perry, according to one official, said his schedule was "flexible" and he was willing to wait until a successor was chosen. Published reports have centred on CIA Director John Deutch as a possible successor.

Perry is considered by many experts to be one of the strongest and most popular Pentagon leaders in decades, despite recent controversies and clashes with Congress over the future role of U.S. forces in Bosnia, the effects of Iraqi chemical weapons on U.S. Gulf War troops and responsibility for two bombings in Saudi Arabia that killed 24 U.S. troops.

"When I became the secretary of defence, I came in with a strong commitment to approach defence from a bipartisan view, to work very, very closely on a bipartisan basis with the Congress," Perry said in response to questions during an appearance at U.S. Strategic Command headquarters at Offutt.
"In the first few years, I think, I was very successful in doing that. In the last year or so, it has been very difficult to work on a bipartisan basis with the Congress," he added.

"There has been a much stronger partisan approach to defence issues. And this, I think, has been a problem. I think it can very well decrease the capability of the United States to conduct a well-organised, well-managed defence programme."

The news that Perry planned to leave came on the heels of statements from State Department officials that Secretary of State Warren Christopher had resigned his post and would leave before Clinton begins his second term in January.

"I don't think there is any good time or bad time walking away from the job as secretary of defence," Perry told reporters who travelled with him to Europe last month. "There is always a problem. There is always a crisis. There's always some programme that is halfway completed."

Perry, who has nurtured close ties with senior defence officials in Russia and other former Soviet communist states, rose from the post of deputy defence secretary in early 1994 to take the top job after the late Defence Secretary Les Aspin resigned under pressure.
Since then he has undertaken a crushing work and travel schedule that would leave many less active persons exhausted.

There was no immediate indication of who might succeed Perry. But reports have prominently mentioned Deutch, who served as deputy defence secretary before moving to the CIA last year, and retiring Georgia Sen. Sam Nunn.

Retiring Republican Sen. William Cohen of Maine has also emerged in reports as a possible candidate. Deputy Attorney General Jamie Gorelick, who previously served as the Pentagon's top lawyer, has made no secret she would like the job.

Perry, in response to questions from reporters last month, expressed pride in initiatives under him to slash nuclear weapons in the United States and former Soviet Union, to improve support for military personnel and reform the way the Pentagon buys arms and equipment.

"I should, for point of reference, say that I had not decided to take this job in the first place. It was not something I sought, something I was anxious to do," Perry said. "It was something which was urged on me and after a lot of consideration I finally decided to do."
